title: DP IV: Bitmask & Digit DP — Depth Pass
relevance: Medium — second wave after Matching / Elevator / Classy Numbers / TSP; these are the CF Div2 D–E and ABC E drills that hide mask packing, profile DP, and digit-bound construction rather than announcing the template.
company_notes: OA/interview shapes: visit k POIs or playlists with genre rules (shortest paths/adjacency then Hamiltonian mask DP); count valid strings/colorings with local forbidden patterns (last few symbols packed as a mask); largest arrangement or next number under digit constraints (left-to-right under an upper bound); assign a tiny set of skills/problems/medicines (2^n over the skill mask, often after sorting an external cost dimension).

phases.goal: Spot hidden bitmask or digit DP from tiny universes, numeric digit invariants, or thin-grid column fills rather than an announced template.

must_hit.point: Depth states still look like dp[mask], dp[mask][last], or dfs(pos,tight,extra), but contests hide the template behind tiny dimensions or a huge numeric bound with a digit property.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate names mask/TSP/digit-tight shapes and says the hard part is the non-obvious extra (APSP before TSP, topo checks, AND shrinkage, profile compatibility, product IDs).

must_hit.point: Recognize when brute subsets or 2^n·n^2 fits, when [L,R] is up to 10^18 with a digit property, or when a thin grid forces filling one column or one mask at a time.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives at least one of: subset/2^n fit, digit-range bound, or thin-grid column-mask cue.

must_hit.point: Tiny-universe cue: n≤20, k≤10 specials, width ≤3–8, ≤10 factorials, or ≤16 rows often means mask packing rather than a named DP chapter.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites those constraint families as the tell that a mask or column profile will fit.

probes: What constraint or story cues would make you reach for bitmask DP or digit DP here instead of plain memo on indices?

hints.1: Look past the story for a tiny set size or a digit-bound numeric range.
hints.2: Ask whether a subset of specials, a column of width a few cells, or digits of a bound up to 10^18 is the real state.
hints.3: If 2^n·n^2 fits, [L,R] has a digit invariant, or the grid is thin enough to fill one column mask at a time, name dp[mask]/dp[mask][last]/dfs(pos,tight,extra).

phases.goal: Choose the right depth-pass reduction: specials-then-TSP, topo mask, AND/OR shrinkage, bit-greedy oracle, BS+coordinate mask, product compression, or thin-grid profile.

must_hit.point: Specials-then-TSP: when only k≤20 keys matter on a big graph, BFS/APSP among keys first, then dp[mask][i] on the complete digraph.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States reduce-to-keys then Hamiltonian mask DP (Magical Ornament / Playlist shape).

must_hit.point: Topo mask: dp[mask] adds from dp[mask^1<<v] only if every prerequisite of v already lies in mask^1<<v (counting linear extensions).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explains prerequisite check before placing v into the set mask.

must_hit.point: AND/OR shrinkage keeps state in 2^{bitwidth}: iterate new = old & a[i], or check a[i] under a candidate OR mask — bits only disappear.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions Don't Blame Me–style AND transitions or Boboniu-style candidate OR feasibility.

must_hit.point: Bit-greedy + oracle: fix answer bits MSB→LSB and use a segment/partition DP only to ask whether frozen high bits are still realizable — do not DP the full numeric answer.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes Bookshelves-style MSB decisions with a feasibility oracle.

must_hit.point: BS + coordinate mask: threshold x turns each vector into a bitset of good coordinates; feasibility is an OR cover of (1<<m)-1 (often two masks).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Binary-searches x, packs coords ≥x into masks, checks full OR coverage.

probes: Walk through how you would reduce Magical Ornament or Footrace before writing the mask DP transitions.

hints.1: Separate graph reduction or ordering constraints from the mask recurrence itself.
hints.2: For POIs: APSP on specials then TSP; for topo: only add a vertex when all prereqs are already in the prior mask.
hints.3: State Magical Ornament as BFS/APSP on ≤10 keys then dp[mask][i]; Footrace as dp[mask] ways with prerequisite gates on mask^1<<v.

phases.goal: Encode digit DP extras (used-digit mask, product/sum IDs) and thin-grid column profiles with correct transition filters.

must_hit.point: Digit product/sum compression: map every reachable product or digit-sum to a dense ID before memoizing — raw product explodes.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions Digit Products / Travelling Salesman Special Numbers style ID compression in the DFS/memo key.

must_hit.point: Used-digit mask inside digit DP: for ≤k distinct digits or minimize distinct digits in a range, keep mask of digits used so far plus tight.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names tight + used-digit mask (Unlucky Numbers family).

must_hit.point: Thin-grid profile: width w≤8 or n≤3 ⇒ process the long direction; state is occupancy/colors of the previous column; reject incompatible 2×2 or run patterns.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes column-mask DP with 2×2/run filters (505 / Barcode / Bicolorings).

must_hit.point: Pure forbidden-digit skeleton is (pos,tight,leading); last few symbols can be packed as a small mask or base-4 state for local forbidden patterns.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites Forbidden Digits skeleton and We Like AGC–style last-3 packing.

probes: How do you keep digit-product state small, and what extra do you store for minimize-distinct-digits in [L,R]?

hints.1: The memo key needs more than position and tight when the invariant is product or used digits.
hints.2: Compress reachable products/sums to dense IDs; for distinct-digit goals add a used-digit mask.
hints.3: Digit Products: map products to ≤ a few thousand IDs; Unlucky Numbers: tight + used-mask; thin grids: previous-column mask with 2×2 parity/run checks.

phases.goal: Justify that the chosen mask/digit/profile state fits the constraints named in the depth-pass pattern.

must_hit.point: Classic fit check: brute subsets or 2^n·n^2 must fit the tiny universe before committing to mask DP.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Ties feasibility to 2^n·n^2 or subset enumeration on the stated tiny n/k.

must_hit.point: Medicine/disease-style graphs explore on the order of 2^n·m edges over cured-bit masks (Dijkstra/0-1 BFS).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States shortest path over disease/medicine masks with 2^n·m edges.

must_hit.point: Prereq ladder already includes submask enumeration O(3^n); depth problems reuse that budget when transitions iterate submasks or small specials.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions O(3^n) submask work as the known budget when applicable.

probes: Before coding, how do you argue the mask or digit state will finish under the given limits?

hints.1: Count what the mask indexes: vertices, specials, bits, or column cells.
hints.2: Compare against 2^n·n^2 fit, 2^n·m edge walks, or digit DFS with compressed extras.
hints.3: Say: if subsets/2^n·n^2 fit, or specials are ≤10/k≤20 after APSP, or column mask is 2^n with n≤3, the depth state is justified.

phases.goal: Avoid depth-pass failure modes: full-answer DP instead of bit-greedy, uncompressed products, missing topo gates, or skipping the APSP reduction.

must_hit.point: Do not DP the full numeric answer when bit-greedy + partition oracle can freeze MSB bits and only check realizability.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Corrects Bookshelves-style mistakes: MSB→LSB with feasibility DP, not value-as-state.

must_hit.point: Do not memoize raw digit products — compress reachable products (or digit-sums) to dense IDs first.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Flags product explosion and states ID mapping before memo.

must_hit.point: Topo mask transitions that omit the prerequisite-in-prior-mask check overcount linear extensions.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Requires every prerequisite of v in mask^1<<v before adding ways.

must_hit.point: Hamiltonian mask DP on all vertices fails when only k specials matter — reduce with BFS/APSP among keys first.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Insists on specials-then-TSP, not TSP on the full graph.

probes: What goes wrong if you put the numeric answer in the DP state for Bookshelves, or skip APSP before Magical Ornament’s mask DP?

hints.1: Depth bugs are usually wrong reduction or wrong extra in the state, not missing the word mask.
hints.2: Check whether bits should be frozen greedily, products compressed, prereqs gated, or the graph reduced to keys.
hints.3: Bookshelves: MSB oracle not full-answer DP; Digit Products: dense IDs; Footrace: prereq gate; Magical Ornament: APSP on ≤10 keys then dp[mask][i].

tradeoffs.topic: Specials-then-TSP vs Hamiltonian mask DP on the full vertex set
tradeoffs.strong_answer: When only k specials/POIs matter on a large graph, BFS/APSP among keys then dp[mask][i] on the complete digraph; masking all vertices is the wrong universe.

tradeoffs.topic: Bit-greedy + partition oracle vs DP over the full numeric answer
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Decide answer bits MSB→LSB and only ask a segment/partition DP whether frozen high bits remain realizable; do not put the whole numeric answer in the DP state.

tradeoffs.topic: Dense product/sum IDs vs memoizing raw digit products
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Raw product explodes; map every reachable product or digit-sum to a dense ID before memoizing (Digit Products / popcount-chain digit DP).

tradeoffs.topic: Thin-grid column profile vs cell-by-cell state
tradeoffs.strong_answer: When width w≤8 or n≤3, process the long direction with previous-column occupancy/color mask and reject incompatible 2×2 or run patterns.

tradeoffs.topic: Iterate/binary-search OR or threshold candidates vs searching the full answer space
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Boboniu-style: iterate possible OR values and check each a_i hits some b_j under the candidate; Minimax-style: binary-search x, pack coords ≥x into masks, require OR cover of (1<<m)-1.

gotchas.trap: Treating Bookshelves as DP over the full numeric answer.
gotchas.correction: Fix bits from MSB to LSB; use partition DP only as an oracle that the frozen high-bit prefix is still achievable with k segments.

gotchas.trap: Memoizing digit-product directly in Digit Products-style problems.
gotchas.correction: Compress every reachable product to a dense ID (≤ a few thousand) before including it in the digit-DP state.

gotchas.trap: Adding a vertex to a topo mask without checking prerequisites.
gotchas.correction: Only transition dp[mask] from dp[mask^1<<v] when every prerequisite of v already lies in mask^1<<v.

gotchas.trap: Running TSP mask DP on the entire map for k POIs.
gotchas.correction: BFS/APSP among the ≤10 (or k≤20) keys first, then Hamiltonian dp[mask][i] on that complete digraph.

gotchas.trap: Forgetting that AND transitions only shrink bits.
gotchas.correction: new = old & a[i] (or checks against a candidate OR) keeps the state space inside 2^{bitwidth}; do not reinvent a larger combinatorial state.

gotchas.trap: Minimizing distinct digits in [L,R] with only (pos,tight).
gotchas.correction: Carry a used-digit mask alongside tight so the distinct-digit invariant is in the state.
